builder_plan.scenario: A multi-step product task fails because the agent loses track of dependencies.
builder_plan.change: Try the proposed planning step on tasks with checkable intermediate outcomes.
builder_plan.baseline: The same agent solving the same tasks without the new planning step.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task completion, unnecessary steps, planning tokens, response time, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: OSGR: Observation-Support Graph Reasoning for Earth Observation Question Answering
summary: OSGR replaces unconstrained LLM-agent search over Earth observation archives with a two-stage factorization: an offline Observation-Support Graph deduces valid concept-level support paths, and online Relation-Conditioned Grounding instantiates items under spatiotemporal compatibility kernels. The cost is building and maintaining the offline symbolic graph plus a domain-specific grounding pipeline, which is engineering effort orthogonal to general-purpose workloads. It can fail where the offline graph lacks coverage of required concepts or relations, and its gains are demonstrated only on EO benchmarks, so transfer to other retrieval-and-derivation domains is unverified.
rationale: The method addresses a niche Earth-observation QA problem requiring a domain-specific symbolic graph that a small team with constrained infrastructure cannot justify building unless EO is their production domain.
technique: Offline support-graph grounding for EO QA

claims.statement: OSGR replaces unconstrained LLM-agent search over Earth observation archives with a two-stage factorization: an offline Observation-Support Graph deduces valid concept-level support paths, and online Relation-Conditioned Grounding instantiates items under spatiotemporal compatibility kernels. The cost is building and maintaining the offline symbolic graph plus a domain-specific grounding pipeline, which is engineering effort orthogonal to general-purpose workloads. It can fail where the offline graph lacks coverage of required concepts or relations, and its gains are demonstrated only on EO benchmarks, so transfer to other retrieval-and-derivation domains is unverified.
On Earth-Bench and DisasterM3-Reason, OSGR raises GPT-4o accuracy from 49.3% to 63.7% and reduces the execution-step ratio from 2.9 to 2.5.
